subject: Counter-sign request: limited runtime telemetry carveout for EdgePilot integration
messages:
From: Simon Reynolds <simon@edgepilot.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: legal@edgepilot.com, eng@edgepilot.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: EdgePilot DPA proposed carveout for runtime telemetry

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our engineering team's ask, we've attached a proposed DPA redline that includes a narrow carveout to allow short-term, aggregated runtime telemetry exports to our analytics partner (AnalyticaLabs) solely for model ranking improvement. The main points:

- Exported data would be anonymized and rate-limited; no raw prompts stored long-term.
- Retention on EdgePilot's side: max 14 days for the aggregated artifacts.
- Subprocessor: AnalyticaLabs (US-only), SOC 2 Type II attested.

We included suggested language to limit scope to: "non-personally-identifying operational metrics and model ranking signals derived from ephemeral runtime metadata." Please have your product/security teams review and let us know if we can proceed to countersign.

Attachments: EdgePilot_DPA_redline_v2.pdf, ep-runtime-path-diagram.png

Happy to hop on a quick call if it helps.

— Simon
Head of Partnerships, EdgePilot

Folks — forwarding EdgePilot's redline. They want a narrow export path to AnalyticaLabs for model ranking signals. High-level ask from me: can Security + Product sign off on a conditional carveout with our controls, or do we require a flat rejection?

Quick context: this is an integration pilot (deal EP-4321) and they are asking for a short retention window (14 days) and anonymization language. Potential product impacts include additional batching/guardrails around token sampling and a small increase in egress/obs costs.

Please review the attached redline and the diagram. Questions I have:
- Is the proposed "non-personally-identifying" phrasing acceptable to Legal/Security?
- Do we need a stricter retention window or specific encryption/KMS language?
- If we approve, what addenda/controls do we require in the contract or operational runbook?

Next steps I propose: Security provides annotated change suggestions; Product proposes implementation constraints (rate limits, sampling thresholds); Legal finalizes countersign language and DocuSign flow.

If you prefer, we can schedule 30m tomorrow to resolve.

— Kimberly
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EdgePilot DPA proposed carveout for runtime telemetry

Kimberly / Karthik —

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed the redline and the diagram. High-level security position: we may be able to accept a narrowly-scoped telemetry carveout if the following conditions are contractually required and operationally enforced:

- Data scope: explicit list of allowed telemetry fields (no user prompt text, no identifiers, no full request/response pairs).
- Anonymization: strong hashing & tokenization prior to any export; no reversible mapping stored by EdgePilot.
- Retention: reduce to 7 days on their side (14 days is higher risk; 7 days acceptable for ranking experiments).
- Subprocessor assurance: AnalyticaLabs must provide SOC 2 Type II report and a data processing addendum; we require SSP contact for periodic audit status.
- Encryption: exports must be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest with customer-provided KMS option for enterprise customers (if requested).
- Access controls: exports accessible only to named engineers via least-privilege roles; CI/CD keys rotated quarterly.

Suggested redline bullets (to Legal):
1) Add explicit field-level whitelist and prohibition on prompt/response contents.
2) Lower retention to 7 days and require purge evidence on request.
3) Require AnalyticaLabs SOC 2 upload within 10 business days and contractually-binding notification on any control lapses.

I'll attach a short annotated PDF with inline changes for Legal to consume (KP_annotated_redline_comments.pdf). From an operational standpoint, we'll need Product to scope required telemetry trimming and sampling behavior.

If Product confirms feasibility, Security can sign off conditionally and Legal can prepare the countersign language. I am not comfortable with an open-ended "non-personally-identifying" phrase alone — it is too vague.

— Olga
Senior Product Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, legal@edgepilot.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EdgePilot DPA proposed carveout for runtime telemetry

Thanks Olga — good, concrete feedback. Quick Product reply:

Feasibility notes:
- We can implement a field-level whitelist at inference ingress that strips prompt text and only emits metric-derived signals (e.g., response latency, token-level ranking features, hashed feature vectors).
- Sampling: we'll add a default 1% sampling rate for the pilot and allow EdgePilot to request increases via tracked change requests (subject to approval).
- Retention: lowering to 7 days is fine. We'll also provide a purge API that Legal/Security can call to verify deletion on demand.
- KMS: we can support enterprise KMS for select customers; for this pilot we'll require EdgePilot to use their provider-managed keys and provide proof of rotation schedule.

Operational asks for contract language:
- Field whitelist + ban on prompt/response storage.
- Explicit sampling cap (1% default) and an approval path for increases.
- 7-day retention and purge API SLA (48 hours for purge confirmation).
- SOC 2 attestation required for their analytics subprocessor.

If Security is comfortable with those contract changes, Legal please prepare countersign wording and procurement can route to DocuSign. Kimberly — feel free to confirm and I can draft a short tech note for their engineering team so they can implement with minimal back-and-forth.

— Karthik
Product Manager, Integrations | Redwood Inference
